claim.quote: With a 3.7 g NaI crystal, e$^-$/$\gamma$ events could be clearly distinguished from nuclear recoils down to the nuclear recoil energy threshold of 15 keV.

name: Particle discrimination in a NaI crystal using the COSINUS remote TES design

summary.plain: A 3.7 g sodium iodide crystal cooled to millikelvin temperatures, read out through COSINUS's remote sensor design, could tell electron events from nuclear recoils above 15 keV, in an above-ground test.
summary.technical: remoTES NaI prototype operated above ground for 9.06 g d: event-by-event e/gamma versus nuclear-recoil discrimination in the dual phonon plus light read-out down to a nuclear-recoil threshold of 15 keV (Phys. Rev. D 109, 082003).

title: Particle discrimination in a NaI crystal using the COSINUS remote TES design
why_it_matters: Particle discrimination in NaI is what lets COSINUS separate nuclear recoils from the electron background that DAMA/LIBRA cannot reject.
